ref: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.1
stem: Find the value of the discriminant of the equation \(x^2 + 10x - 7 = 0\)

ref: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.2 (i)
context: Determine nature of roots of the quadratic equations.
setLabel: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.2
solution:
Compare \(2x^2 - 5x + 7 = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\)

\(a = 2\), \(b = -5\), \(c = 7\),

\(\therefore\) \(b^2 - 4ac = (-5)^2 - 4 \times 2 \times 7\)

\(D = 25 - 56\)

\(D = -31\)

\(\therefore\) \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\)

\(\therefore\) the roots of the equation are not real.

ref: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.2 (ii)
context: Determine nature of roots of the quadratic equations.
setLabel: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.2
solution:
Compare \(x^2 + 2x - 9 = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\).

\(a = 1\), \(b = 2\), \(c = -9\),

\(\therefore\) \(b^2 - 4ac = 2^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-9)\)

\(D = 4 - (-36)\)

\(D = 40\)

\(\therefore\) \(b^2 - 4ac > 0\)

\(\therefore\) the roots of the equation are real and unequal.

ref: Nature of roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.3
solution:
Compare \(\sqrt{3}\,x^2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,x + \sqrt{3} = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\)

We get \(a = \sqrt{3}\), \(b = 2\sqrt{3}\), \(c = \sqrt{3}\),

\(\therefore\) \(b^2 - 4ac = (2\sqrt{3})^2 - 4 \times \sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}\)

\(= 4 \times 3 - 4 \times 3\)

\(= 12 - 12\)

\(= 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\)

\(\therefore\) Roots of the equation are real and equal.
